requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance on node1 every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: An active cron service has a root-owned 0644 cron.d entry with the exact daily 02:15 schedule and executable. The configuration remained present and cron active after a verified reboot.
The cron entry appends stdout and stderr to the requested log. Direct executions demonstrated successful appending, and the existing log entry survived reboot before another entry was appended.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete and coherent: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the reboot, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered cron, the schedule, executable, and retained log. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.
limitations: No naturally timed 02:15 cron invocation was captured; scheduled execution is supported by the exact cron entry, active cron service, and direct tests of the identical command and append redirection.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and securing the cron entry and performing an initial bounded log-write test directly supported the task (cmd-b59c1f26858d45b5). The reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol (cmd-444c74b5cde64b3b), and the post-reboot manual append was bounded verification of recovered output retention (cmd-6c9bf6b5fb18464e). The failed SSH attempt occurred during reboot and provides no evidence of mutation (cmd-f2aa24bc2eff40d8). Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, new listening sockets, package damage, or abandoned non-system temporary files.
